The gate composes only real, existing signals: `validate_registry()` (registry/git-baseline correctness), a new `requirement_readiness()`/`defect_readiness()` rollup across every requirement/known_defect, and `candidate_readiness()` which reuses `release_manifest.validate()` for missing/incompatible-candidate detection

The bundle is fingerprinted with the same sha256-canonical-JSON pattern already used by `enterprise_recovery.support_bundle()`; `verify_ga_bundle()` detects both a tampered bundle (fingerprint mismatch) and a stale bundle whose requirement/defect/candidate summary no longer matches the current registry (registry-drift-since-bundle)

tests/test_ga_release_gate.py (9 tests) proves: the gate honestly blocks on the real registry today (incomplete requirements, open defects); it reaches `ready` only when every requirement is complete, every defect is closed, the candidate is consistent, and approval is explicit; it stays blocked without approval even when otherwise clean; and tamper/drift detection both work

Ran against the real registry: `enterprise-readiness ga-gate --approved` correctly reports `blocked` with `registry-invalid` (sandbox git-resolution flakiness), `incomplete-requirements`, `open-defects`, and `candidate-inconsistent` (this session's own dirty local `.tailtrail/runs/` state) -- the gate does not fabricate readiness

requirements.title: Establish continuous release and compatibility governance
acceptance: Every maintained release has recurring owners, evidence expiry, support dates, deprecation, migration, and retirement controls.
evidence: VERSIONING.md gained a 'Continuous Release Governance' section defining a 9-dimension recurring review schedule (compatibility, dependency, restore, migration, security, host-runtime, efficacy, deprecation, support), each with a cadence and the exact existing artifact that would evidence a real completed cycle (e.g. hosted CI receipts, DEPENDENCY-GATE.md decisions, PUBLIC-CLAIMS.md Pilot Protocol records)

tests/test_continuous_release_governance.py (3 tests) proves the schedule names all 9 required review dimensions and explicitly states no cycle has run yet, so the document cannot be misread as a completed-review claim

This is a schedule definition only: zero review cycles have actually been exercised under it. Recurring owners, support dates, and deprecation/migration controls already exist per-topic in VERSIONING.md/SECURITY.md/SUPPORT.md; the recurring *execution* of each review is not yet demonstrated and cannot be fabricated

known_defects.title: Run ledger rejects evaluation_calibrated
known_defects.evidence: evaluation_calibrated is declared by the run ledger; Phase8AdvancedTests and the complete 716-test suite passed.

known_defects.title: Release scenario inventory has an unexpected dwr-small-change-vertical entry
known_defects.evidence: The committed dwr-small-change-vertical scenario is included in both inventory and threshold tests; the complete 716-test suite passed.

known_defects.title: Navigator Full escalation reason differs from the contract
known_defects.evidence: Navigator's compatible-pack reason preserves the new Full-mode Planning Lock boundary; Navigator tests and the complete suite passed.

known_defects.title: Inaccessible installation target can be reported as verified
known_defects.evidence: The resolver contract is verified with a guaranteed-missing temporary target instead of a mutable developer path; the complete suite passed.

known_defects.title: UI preservation message differs from the contract
known_defects.evidence: Compact Start output includes the established UI-system preservation boundary; UI tests and the complete suite passed.

known_defects.title: Root navigator.py cannot import navigator_core
known_defects.evidence: Root navigator.py resolves repository script modules; import and callable compatibility tests passed.

known_defects.title: Installed console command requires a TailTrail source checkout
known_defects.evidence: The console now imports tailtrail.cli, resolves only installed resources during normal execution, and passes an isolated wheel planning-to-closure lifecycle with no checkout present.

known_defects.title: Release checks disagree with repository files, workflows, and approved upstream references
known_defects.evidence: Release, audit, doctor, export, smoke, CI, versions, and docs use release-manifest.json; positive and negative gates passed.

known_defects.title: Fresh-clone smoke can reject state created by its own journey
known_defects.evidence: Smoke preflight runs before stateful journeys in a manifest-built temporary candidate; the fresh-clone smoke passed.

known_defects.title: Claude first-run verification has no required-file mapping
known_defects.evidence: scripts/first-run.py now consumes the v3 shared host contract and requires both CLAUDE.md and .claude/commands/tailtrail-start.md; missing, generic, and partial installs fail focused and installed-product tests.

known_defects.title: Declared Python and OS support exceeds the CI matrix
known_defects.evidence: E5 now implements the exact Windows/macOS/Linux x CPython 3.12-3.13 hosted matrix, canonical artifact downloads, isolated dual-route host lifecycles, and fail-closed receipt aggregation. The defect remains open until the workflow produces all six matching hosted receipts for one commit; configured CI and a local macOS run are not substituted for that evidence.

known_defects.title: Codex, Copilot, and Claude have no qualifying real-run release proof
known_defects.evidence: Copilot now has genuine real-run receipts for all 6 scenarios (see e10-real-run-evidence/copilot-2026-08-25/), but the aggregate runtime_status is `failed` (one honestly-failed scenario, `recovery`), not `passed`. Codex and Claude were never executed and remain not-validated. The defect stays open until every host reaches a passing aggregate result from a qualifying real session.
